clue.text: Bouncer, saving time, bad spy tailed?

indicators.note: saving means keeping hold of, so the word for bad holds the time letter inside it

parts.note: poor means bad, of low quality
the spy is James Bond, 007; tailed means docked of its tail, so the final 7 goes and 00 is read as the letters OO

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer, short on time, is shadowing a hopeless secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' looks like a doorman, but it is the definition: a hopping marsupial. 'saving' puts T inside POOR to give POTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The potoroo is a small Australian rat-kangaroo that moves by hopping, so it is literally a bouncer.

clue.text: Mediocre writing by a follower of Oscar

parts.note: pap is worthless, trivial reading matter

explanation.surface: Second-rate prose produced by a disciple of Wilde.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests Wilde, but in the NATO phonetic alphabet Oscar (O) is followed by Papa (P).
explanation.definitionFit: In the international radio alphabet the code word for P comes straight after the code word for O.

clue.text: Batter who makes test runs all the time

definitions.text: Batter who makes test runs all the time

parts.words: Batter who makes test runs all the time
parts.note: a batsman forever scoring runs in Test matches; the nickname belongs to India's Sachin Tendulkar (and earlier Pakistan's Hanif Mohammad)

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, Test matches are international games; 'test runs' also suggests trial runs to throw you.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname was given to short but prolific Test batsmen, most famously Sachin Tendulkar, the leading run-scorer in Test history.

clue.text: Cut away some of trees out of control around castle

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the castle's letter
out of control suggests letters running wild into a new order

parts.note: C is given in Chambers as an abbreviation for castle, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A gardener lops trees that have grown wild around a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of control' turns TREES into RESET, and 'around' puts C inside to give RESE-C-T.
explanation.definitionFit: To resect is a surgical term for cutting out part of an organ or tissue.

clue.text: Books belonging to Esther or Ruth, say — or those not yet mentioned

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books

parts.words: belonging to Esther or Ruth, say
parts.note: something belonging to any woman, such as Esther or Ruth, is hers

explanation.surface: Biblical books named after Esther or Ruth, set against the rest of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Esther and Ruth are Old Testament books, which steers you to scripture; here they are just two women's names.
explanation.definitionFit: The others means the remaining people or things, those not already named.

clue.text: British PM's obvious success

definitions.note: the possessive 's is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a bald statement is a plain, obvious one
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister's victory is there for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was a British Conservative Prime Minister three times between the wars; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin led three British governments in the 1920s and 1930s, a historical holder of the premiership.

clue.text: Head up, in maintaining current easy disposition

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the word for in keeps the current symbol inside

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Keep your chin up and stay cheerful, an easygoing attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head up' reads as encouragement, but in a down clue 'up' reverses the slang for head, giving BON; 'maintaining' wraps the home word around the current symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful friendliness, a good-natured, easygoing temperament.

clue.text: Short, general email off the subject

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: gen is short for general

explanation.surface: A brief, general message that strays from the topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges GEN and EMAIL together; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman was a vassal sworn to serve a feudal lord, that is, a loyal subject.

clue.text: Throwaway remark?

parts.note: throwaway usually means casual, but here it is a remark about throwing things away, a proverb against wastefulness

explanation.walkthrough: A 'throwaway remark' is an offhand comment; the question mark invites reading it as a saying about not discarding things.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns that if you do not squander things you will not go short, a comment on throwing away.

clue.text: Ice cream for the perspiring parts of genius?

definitions.text: Ice cream for the perspiring parts of genius?

parts.words: Ice cream for the perspiring parts of genius?
parts.note: a 99 is a British ice-cream cone with a chocolate flake; Edison said genius is one per cent inspiration and the remaining hundredths perspiration

explanation.walkthrough: A 99 is a British soft-serve cone with a chocolate flake; Edison's saying gives perspiration that share of genius.
explanation.definitionFit: The ice-cream name and the percentage of genius Edison put down to sweat share the same number.

clue.text: Journalists hurry

definitions.meaning: the ... collectively means reporters and the newspapers they write for
to ... on or ... ahead is to hurry, urge forward

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: newspaper people as a body, and a verb for pushing on urgently.

clue.text: The Rain King is, they conclude, in love

indicators.note: in places the phrase for those who conclude within the word for a loved one

parts.note: hon, short for honey, is a term of endearment for a loved one
those who end something are enders

explanation.surface: A mythic rain-maker turns out, in the end, to be smitten.
explanation.walkthrough: Saul Bellow's novel is 'Henderson the Rain King'; Henderson is also the setter Enigmatist's surname, a little self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Henderson is the hero of Saul Bellow's novel, who is acclaimed by an African tribe as their rain king.

clue.text: Double manoeuvre against province men met with calamity

indicators.note: meeting with calamity suggests these words are wrecked and thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A two-pronged military operation against a region's men ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: PROVINCE, MEN and MET together give exactly the fourteen letters; 'against' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pincer movement attacks an enemy from both flanks at once, a two-sided manoeuvre in military tactics.

clue.text: Under counter, old drunken farts won sham argument

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the rest is written below the counter

parts.note: a man is a piece or counter in board games such as draughts

indicators.note: drunken suggests these letters are reeling about out of order

parts.note: W stands for won in sports results tables

explanation.surface: Beneath the bar, an old drunk breaks wind and claims victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges FARTS to FSTRA, which with O and W gives OFSTRAW below MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of straw is a weak or misrepresented argument set up only to be knocked down.

clue.text: Aesthetic or non-aesthetic? He's gone for the former

indicators.note: he's gone says the letters of the pronoun leave the word for a non-aesthete

parts.note: at Oxbridge, hearties (sporty, boisterous types) were the traditional opposite of aesthetes
the pronoun he, its 's read as 'has', taken literally as the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether someone is cultured or a philistine, settled by his departure.
explanation.walkthrough: The old university division between hearties (games players) and aesthetes (the arty set) supplies the opposite; 'for the former' points back to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone with artistic pretensions, the aesthetic type set against the sporty set.

clue.text: Rogue "repaired" air con, trapping oxygen; there's little change ahead

indicators.note: ahead says the small coin's letter is placed at the very front of the rest

parts.note: p stands for penny, a small coin, the smallest change

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the reworked letters enclose the gas's symbol
repaired, in quotes, suggests the letters have been put back together in a fresh order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A crooked tradesman botches an air-conditioning job and pockets a few pennies first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges AIR CON to ICARON, and 'trapping' puts O inside it to make ICAROON.
explanation.definitionFit: A picaroon is an archaic word for a rogue, rascal or pirate, from Spanish picarón.

clue.text: Ding-dong involving Johnny Green and Tommy Stout in fortunate circumstances?

parts.words: involving Johnny Green and Tommy Stout
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Ding Dong Bell, little Johnny Green put pussy in the well and little Tommy Stout pulled her out
a ding-dong is a noisy row, a to-do

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme commotion over a cat that ends happily.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs 'Ding dong bell, pussy's in the well'; 'Ding-dong' doubles as a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do means prosperous, comfortably off, which is a fortunate position to be in.

clue.text: Blasts upwards and pierces flag

indicators.note: pierces means the joining word goes into the middle of the other piece
in a down clue, upwards means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: drats, like blast, is a mild curse

explanation.surface: Explosions shoot skywards and tear through a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwards' reverses the mild curse to give STARD, and 'pierces' drives the joining word into its middle; 'Blasts' looks like explosions but is an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner, especially one carried into battle or flown as an emblem.

clue.text: Work to repeat work

indicators.note: to work something is to knead and reshape it, so the following letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An instruction to do a task over again.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Work' is the anagram signal and the second is the definition; TO REPEAT rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light comic opera, a musical work for the stage.

clue.text: Gem?

parts.note: Gem is short for Gemini; the question mark asks for one of them, a single member of the pair

explanation.walkthrough: Gem reads as a jewel, but here it is the abbreviation of Gemini, the zodiac sign of the Twins.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is the constellation of the heavenly twins Castor and Pollux, so a shortened Gemini suggests one of them.

clue.text: Energy packs divers never finish

indicators.note: packs means is packed into, so the energy letter goes inside
divers is an old word for various or several, so the letters are scattered differently

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An energy bar keeps scuba divers going so they never tire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' rearranges NEVER to VENER, and E goes inside to make VENEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin surface layer of fine wood or other material, a finish applied over cheaper stuff.

clue.text: Floor formation, not a little camp

indicators.note: not means without, so the small thing is taken away

parts.note: a stalagmite rises from a cave floor
a mite means a little, a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A cave structure on the ground, not a small one.
explanation.walkthrough: Stalagmites grow up from the floor, stalactites down from the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War.

clue.text: Function involving end of exam: every candidate taking part received a little food course

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the mathematical function wraps around everything else

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

indicators.note: end of says only the final letter of exam is used

parts.note: all means every one
a candidate taking part is in the test, sitting it

explanation.surface: An exam ends with a social function at which every candidate is given a small meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' has the trig function swallow the whole run after its first letter; 'received' is a link word, and 'a little food course' is a witty gloss on the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: The small intestine is the narrower stretch of the gut through which food passes after the stomach, a little alimentary course.

clue.text: Can he?

definitions.meaning: can is slang for a toilet
a male first name, here the setter's own name

explanation.definitionFit: John is American slang for a lavatory, as is can, and it is also a common man's first name.

clue.text: Principle or not a popular order for CAMRA members!

definitions.meaning: the reasoning or principle underlying something

definitions.text: not a popular order for CAMRA members!
definitions.meaning: CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, is a British beer drinkers' group

explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning behind an action, its guiding principle; the second reading splits it into an instruction to limit beer.

clue.text: Slowly responded to some of the advice of Polonius?

definitions.meaning: a musical direction meaning to be played slowly

definitions.text: responded to some of the advice of Polonius?
definitions.meaning: Polonius in Hamlet advises 'Neither a borrower nor a lender be'; someone who took it lent nothing, read as lent followed by O, a zero

explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the Italian tempo marking for a slow pace; the second reading splits it as loaned zero.

clue.text: C-in-C, one taking both sides in rumour

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the word for rumour

parts.note: word, as in 'word has it', means a rumour or report
a means one
the two sides are right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: A commander-in-chief is said to be playing both sides at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' splits the word for rumour after its first letter to take the one and both sides; 'taking' is a link word, and C-in-C means commander-in-chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A warlord is a military commander, often one wielding supreme power over a region, as a commander-in-chief does.

clue.text: Fashionable place to walk along the pier topless

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed from the place's name

parts.words: place to walk along the pier
parts.note: Brighton, a seaside resort on England's south coast, is famous for its pier

explanation.surface: A trendy seaside spot where you might stroll the boardwalk without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside resort in southern England known for its Palace Pier.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-on is informal for fashionably correct in opinions, socially or politically up to date.
